roadmaps.title: Top-5% in 47 engineering domains
roadmaps.description:
Top 5% in all of: Computer science, Data structures and algorithms, Maths, Probability, Statistics, C and C++, Operating systems, Linux, Bash, Network, Python, Java, Rust, Databases, Database architecture, Database administration, Data-intensive systems, Kafka and streaming, Spark and batch processing, Data engineering, DataOps, Data analysis, Data science, Analytics engineering, Cloud data warehouses, Lakehouse platforms, Data orchestration, Data governance and quality, Business intelligence, NoSQL and search, Machine learning, Deep learning, MLOps, Generative AI and LLM engineering, Software engineering, System design, API design, Web development, Docker and Podman, Kubernetes, DevOps, GitOps, Cloud, Infrastructure as code, Observability and SRE, Cybersecurity, DevSecOps.

18 phases, about 4,840 hours at 22 hours a week, from 2026-10-19 (a Monday) to 2031-01-05. Each phase has a project that builds on the previous one, and each domain has its certifications (141 in all, labelled by field and vendor) and project work that proves it. The skills assessment is retaken at every phase's end. 22–26 hours a week, 200 € a month (books, a cloud sandbox, a certification fund, a reward fund).

Weekly rhythm: Monday theory, Tuesday the core track, Wednesday practice, Thursday whichever is behind, Friday spaced tests and 3 DSA problems, Saturday 4 h project + 2 h DSA + 1 h notes, Sunday 3 h project + 2 h reading + 1 h Zettel + the weekly reflection.

skills.title: Data engineering
skills.description: Phases 1, 7, 8, 18. Proof: Google Professional Data Engineer; streamhouse in production; ≥ 3 merged PRs in data OSS.

skills.title: DataOps

skills.title: Data science

skills.title: Machine learning

skills.title: Deep learning

skills.title: DevOps

skills.title: Cloud

skills.title: DevSecOps

skills.title: Technical writing

skills.title: Code review and open source

skills.title: Consistency

skills.title: Learning how to learn
skills.description: Literature notes, permanent notes, spaced tests, interleaving, and a running project.

goal.title: Top-5% in 47 engineering domains

- [ ] Data structures and algorithms: The Stanford Algorithms Specialization certificate, at least 400 LeetCode problems, and a contest rating in the top 5%.
- [ ] Maths: The Mathematics for Machine Learning Specialization certificate (Imperial College London); 6.042J, 18.01, 18.02, 18.06 finals ≥ 80%.
- [ ] Probability: MITx 6.431x verified certificate; Stat 110 final ≥ 80%.
- [ ] Statistics: MITx 18.6501x verified certificate; a Bayesian A/B project.
- [ ] C and C++: C++ Institute CPP certification, CS:APP labs, all BusTub projects, sqlc-cpp clang-tidy clean.
- [ ] Operating systems: The Linux Foundation's Linux kernel development certificate (LFD103) and a patch sent upstream; all MIT 6.1810 xv6 labs pass make grade.
- [ ] Linux: LFCS.
- [ ] Bash: LPIC-1 (its exams cover shell scripting); OverTheWire Bandit 0–33 and a tested, ShellCheck-clean automation library.

- [ ] Databases: Oracle Database SQL Certified Associate (1Z0-071); all CMU 15-445 projects and an advanced SQL portfolio.
- [ ] Database architecture: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Database Engineer; architecture decision records for every streamhouse store.
- [ ] Database administration: EDB PostgreSQL Associate then Professional; PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis, and Cassandra runbooks with recorded failover and restore drills.
- [ ] Data-intensive systems: The Cloud Computing Concepts certificates, parts 1 and 2 (University of Illinois); all MIT 6.5840 labs, DDIA permanent notes.
- [ ] Kafka and streaming: Confluent CCDAK.
- [ ] Spark and batch processing: Databricks Certified Associate Developer for Apache Spark.
- [ ] Data engineering: Google Professional Data Engineer; streamhouse in production; ≥ 3 merged PRs in data OSS.
- [ ] DataOps: Dbt Analytics Engineering and Astronomer Airflow certifications; a merged PR in GX or OpenLineage.
- [ ] Data analysis: Microsoft PL-300 and 3 published analyses (EDA, dashboard, A/B).
- [ ] Data science: The MITx MicroMasters in Statistics and Data Science.
- [ ] Machine learning: MITx 6.86x (in the MicroMasters) and a Kaggle silver medal in a 1,000+ team competition.
- [ ] Deep learning: The DeepLearning.AI Deep Learning Specialization; a GPT trained from scratch and a fine-tuned model served.
- [ ] MLOps: Google Professional Machine Learning Engineer; a model in production with drift monitoring.

- [ ] GitOps: CNCF GitOps Certified Associate (CGOA); every platform-gitops environment rebuilt from its repository alone.
- [ ] Cloud: AWS SAA, Google Cloud ACE, and Azure AZ-104.
- [ ] Cybersecurity: BSCP and OSCP+; all PortSwigger labs; MIT 6.566 labs.
- [ ] DevSecOps: Practical DevSecOps CDP; signed images, SBOMs, and policies gating every deploy.
- [ ] Analytics engineering: dbt Analytics Engineering certification; a Kimball star schema in dbt with tests, docs, contracts, and a semantic layer, deployed by CI.
- [ ] Cloud data warehouses: SnowPro Core then SnowPro Advanced: Data Engineer; the same model run on Snowflake and BigQuery with a cost report.
- [ ] Lakehouse platforms: Databricks Certified Data Engineer Associate then Professional; a medallion lakehouse on Delta and Iceberg.
- [ ] Data orchestration: Astronomer Airflow Fundamentals and DAG Authoring certifications; pipekit, then the platform's DAGs, idempotent and backfillable.
- [ ] Data governance and quality: DAMA CDMP Associate; data contracts, quality checks, lineage, and a catalog on the platform; GDPR handled (IAPP CIPP/E).
- [ ] Infrastructure as code: HashiCorp Terraform Associate; the whole cloud data platform created and destroyed from code, with policy checks in CI.

- [ ] NoSQL and search: MongoDB Associate Developer and Elastic Certified Engineer; a search service over the tech watch, and a graph model in Neo4j.

## Why it matters

Moving from "data engineer who uses the tools" to an engineer who masters every
layer, with external proof for each.

habits.title: Daily study block
habits.stack: After dinner on weekdays; at 09:00 on weekends
habits.cue: At the desk, the phone in another room.
habits.craving: Small daily compounding beats heroic weekends.
habits.two: Open today's first task and do one 25-minute pomodoro: a day counts after 25 focused minutes.
habits.reward: Tick the day and watch the streak grow; +1 rest token every 6 study days (bank up to 4), and streak rewards from the 20 € fund.
habits.identity: I'm someone who studies every day.

habits.title: Daily review: spaced tests and the board
habits.stack: When I sit down for the study block, before new material
habits.craving: Retrieval and spacing make 2.5 years of material stick; without them, phase 1 is gone by phase 4.
habits.two: Answer the oldest due test, then move today's tasks to Doing (15 minutes at most).
habits.reward: A cleared board; new material only once the old is retrieved.

habits.title: Weekly project deep-work session
habits.cue: No notifications, the current phase project open.
habits.craving: Projects turn reading into skill and build the portfolio that proves the top 5%.
habits.two: Pick one project task and run the tests; aim for a 4-hour block that ends with a commit.
habits.reward: Push to GitHub and enjoy the green CI badge; a finished feature earns the afternoon off from theory.

habits.title: Weekly reflection and roadmap check
habits.stack: Sunday, the last hour of the weekend block
habits.craving: A 2.5-year plan only survives if it's re-planned every week.
habits.two: Hours done against 22, what I learned, what's stuck, the token bank, next week's 5–8 tasks. Last Sunday of the month: the roadmap check.

habits.title: One DSA problem
habits.cue: The problem list open in the browser's first tab.
habits.craving: Patterns compound: one problem a day is 365 a year.
habits.two: Read one problem and write its brute force.
habits.reward: Log it, its pattern, and the time it took.
habits.identity: I'm someone who solves a problem every day.

habits.title: Maths exercises
habits.cue: The exercise book open on the desk, a pencil on it.
habits.craving: Maths is learnt with the pencil, not by reading.
habits.reward: Tick it in the problem set; a set done is a milestone step.
habits.identity: I'm someone who does maths every day.

habits.title: Linux and Bash, one thing a day
habits.cue: A terminal opens with the day's man page.
habits.craving: The command line is the engineer's hands.
habits.two: Read one man page section or write one line of a script.
habits.reward: Keep it in the dotfiles repository.
habits.identity: I'm someone who lives in the terminal.

habits.title: Code in the phase's language
habits.stack: After the study block's first pomodoro
habits.cue: The phase's project open in the editor.
habits.craving: Fluency comes from writing, every day.
habits.reward: Commit it; the contribution graph fills.
habits.identity: I'm someone who writes code every day.

habits.title: Read 10 pages of an engineering book
habits.reward: Note one idea in the book's literature note.
habits.identity: I'm someone who reads engineering books.

habits.title: Explain one thing learnt
habits.craving: If you can't explain it simply, you don't know it yet.
habits.two: Write three sentences a beginner would understand.
habits.reward: It becomes a permanent note in the vault.
habits.identity: I'm someone who explains what they learn.

habits.title: Sleep 7.5 hours: lights out by 23:00
habits.cue: The bedroom cool and dark, the alarm set for 7.5 hours later.
habits.craving: Memory consolidates during sleep: no sleep, no learning.
habits.two: Be in bed at 22:45, lights off at 23:00.
habits.reward: Note the night's sleep; mornings are sharper.
habits.identity: I'm someone who protects their sleep.

habits.title: Morning sunlight
habits.craving: Light in the eyes in the morning sets the body clock and the evening's sleep.
habits.identity: I'm someone who starts the day outside.

habits.title: Move 30 minutes
habits.stack: After the last call of the day
habits.cue: Walking shoes or the bike ready.
habits.craving: Movement keeps the brain sharp and the back well.
habits.reward: Log it in Health; the week's minutes add up.
habits.identity: I'm someone who moves every day.

habits.title: Strength training
habits.stack: Monday, Wednesday, and Friday before dinner
habits.cue: The mat and the weights out.
habits.craving: Strength keeps a desk worker healthy for decades.
habits.reward: Log the workout; the numbers go up.

habits.title: Drink 2 L of water
habits.stack: At each meal and each study block
habits.cue: A full bottle on the desk.
habits.reward: Log it in Water on Today.
habits.identity: I'm someone who drinks enough water.

habits.title: Screens off an hour before bed
habits.cue: The phone charging outside the bedroom.
habits.craving: Evening light and scrolling push sleep back.
habits.two: Put the phone on its charger.
habits.identity: I'm someone whose evenings are calm.
